findings.who: A filer whose 2024 investment interest was more than their 2024 net investment income, but who filed no 2024 Form 4952. They took the standard deduction, believed the form was not required, or a preparer left it off.
findings.why_no: The outer question asks whether they 'have investment interest expense carried forward from an earlier year'. With no 2024 Form 4952 and no deduction claimed, they believe nothing was 'disallowed' or 'carried forward' and answer no. The inner question's 'what line 7 of a correct 2024 Form 4952 would show' never appears, because the outer no stops the gate first.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 1, line 7: 'Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward to 2026. Subtract line 6 from line 3'; line 2: 'Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7'
findings.fix: Move the fact-based wording into the outer question: 'In 2024 or an earlier year, did you or your spouse have interest on money borrowed for investments (including margin interest or interest shown on a Schedule K-1) that was more than your investment income, even if you filed no Form 4952 or took the standard deduction?'

findings.who: A filer whose only investment interest in 2024 was margin interest on a brokerage statement, or investment interest passed through on a partnership or S corporation Schedule K-1. Some of it was disallowed on the 2024 Form 4952 that their software or preparer produced.
findings.why_no: They never 'borrowed money for investments' in their own view. The K-1 interest was the entity's, and margin is an account feature. The words 'investment interest expense carried forward' do not match anything they remember, so they answer no to both clauses.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: 'Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation'; p. 1, line 2
findings.fix: Name the sources in the gate: 'margin interest on a brokerage account, investment interest shown on a Schedule K-1, or other interest on loans used to buy investments'. Also tell the filer to check line 7 of any 2024 Form 4952 in their return, including forms the software or preparer produced.

findings.who: A filer whose disallowed investment interest arose in 2022 or 2023 and is still unused. Their 2024 return omitted Form 4952 because they had no new investment interest in 2024.
findings.why_no: The gate's line label reads 'Investment interest expense disallowed in 2024 and carried forward'. They had no investment interest in 2024, so nothing was disallowed that year, and they answer no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Who Must File: 'You don't have any carryover of disallowed investment interest expense from 2024'; p. 1, line 7 (carryforward is line 3, which includes line 2's prior carryover, less line 6)
findings.fix: Relabel the gate: 'Investment interest expense disallowed in 2024 or any earlier year and not yet deducted'. State in the outer question that a carryover can persist through years with no new interest and no Form 4952 filed.

findings.who: Any filer shown the outer question. The question ends 'Answer Yes if any of these applies:' but its list does not appear in the gate as reviewed.
findings.why_no: If the list names only current-year borrowing, such as margin loans, a filer with only a carryforward may read the list as the whole rule and answer no.
findings.fix: Make sure the list includes a separate item: 'investment interest you could not deduct in an earlier year (line 7 of a prior Form 4952, or an amount that should have been there)'.

findings.who: A filer, or a spouse on a joint return, owns an interest in a partnership or S corporation, such as a hedge fund, fund of funds or trading partnership, that borrowed to buy securities. The Schedule K-1 reports the filer's share of investment interest expense. The filer personally borrowed nothing.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'you (or ... your spouse) pay interest on money borrowed to buy investments'. The entity borrowed and paid, not the filer, so a truthful answer is no. The help 'Any loan counts if the money went into investments' still reads as the filer's own loan.
findings.line: f4952.line1_if_interest (and, through it, f4952.line4g_if_interest and f4952.carryover_if_interest)
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Include investment interest expense reported to you on Schedule K-1 from a partnership or an S corporation."
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'or does a Schedule K-1 from a partnership or S corporation report investment interest expense to you or your spouse?' Or reword the gate to 'did you or your spouse pay, accrue, or have reported to you on a Schedule K-1 any interest on money borrowed for investments'.

findings.who: A filer who accrued investment interest in 2025 that is properly taken into account for 2025 but was not paid in cash during the year, for example under an accrual method.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether the filer did 'pay interest'. Interest that was accrued but not paid gives a truthful no.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Line 1: "Enter the investment interest expense paid or accrued during the tax year, regardless of when you incurred the indebtedness."
findings.fix: Use 'pay or accrue' in the gate, as the helper condition already does.

findings.who: A filer who borrowed to buy raw land held for appreciation, or who holds a working interest in an oil or gas well directly or through a general partnership without materially participating, and who paid interest on that debt.
findings.why_no: The words 'to buy investments' and the example 'such as a margin loan from a broker' suggest stocks and brokerage accounts. A filer reads land bought on a seller note, or a working interest they see as a business venture, as outside 'investments'.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Property held for investment: "It also includes property that produces gain or loss ... from the disposition of property that ... is held for investment" and "A working interest in an oil or gas property that you held directly or through an entity that didn't limit your liability is property held for investment, but only if you didn't materially participate in the activity."
findings.fix: Widen the examples in the help: 'such as a margin loan, a loan or seller note to buy land held for appreciation, a loan to buy stock or bonds, or a loan to buy an oil or gas working interest you don't actively run'.

findings.who: A filer who paid margin or other investment interest in 2024 or earlier that exceeded that year's net investment income, took the standard deduction, and filed no Form 4952. The carryforward on a correct 2024 line 7 is still available.
findings.why_no: The help says 'Interest of an earlier year counts only if you could not deduct all of it then.' The filer thinks they could have deducted it by itemizing and simply chose not to, so they answer no. The clarifying help about standard-deduction filers appears only on the gated child question, which this filer never sees.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 1, line 7: "Disallowed investment interest expense to be carried forward to 2026. Subtract line 6 from line 3. If zero or less, enter -0-"; line 2: "Disallowed investment interest expense from 2024 Form 4952, line 7"
findings.fix: Move the child's help into the gate: 'Interest of an earlier year counts if it was more than that year's investment income and has not been used since, even if you took the standard deduction or filed no Form 4952.'

findings.who: A filer who borrowed to buy an interest in a partnership or S corporation whose assets are partly investment property, for example an entity holding securities or portfolio assets. Part of the interest on that loan is allocable to property held for investment.
findings.why_no: The filer sees the loan as paying for a share of a business, not for 'investments', and the help speaks only of money that 'went into investments'.
findings.irs_text: f4952 p. 3, Allocation of Interest Expense: "If you paid or accrued interest on a loan and used the loan proceeds for more than one purpose, you may have to allocate the interest ... See ... Notice 89-35"; Line 1: "interest paid or accrued on a loan or part of a loan that is allocable to property held for investment"
findings.fix: Add to the gate help: 'Also answer Yes if you borrowed to buy an interest in a partnership or S corporation that holds stocks, bonds or other investments; part of that interest may count.'
